record.paper_title: Open questions on prominences from coordinated observations by IRIS, Hinode, SDO/AIA, THEMIS, and the Meudon/MSDP
record.original_question: When bubbles and rising plumes are observed in a solar prominence, are they produced by hot plasma that fills a cavity before condensation, by thermal instability, or by magnetic topology such as a separatrix around emerging flux that makes the dark rising structures appear as open windows through the prominence to the background corona?

evidence.quote: Berger et al. (2012) proposed that the bubbles and rising plumes observed with SOT are hot and fill the cavity with plasma before condensation. However, there is a controversy about the existence of thermal instabilities explaining the rising structures in prominences. The bubbles may be due to a separatrix around emerging flux and the dark rising structures just open windows through the prominence, allowing us to see the background corona (Dudík et al. 2012; Gunár et al. 2014).
No study on the temperature and the density of the bubble can be achieved using the IRIS spectra to resolve the question of the existence of a thermal instability.

artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (2019–2025) continues to debate the origin of prominence bubbles and plumes. Multiple mechanisms — magnetic Rayleigh–Taylor and Kelvin–Helmholtz instabilities, magnetic reconnection at separatrices outlining emerging flux, and thermal/condensation processes — are still being proposed and modeled, often as complementary rather than mutually exclusive. No single mechanism has been definitively confirmed as the unique origin, so the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Solar Prominence Bubble and Plumes Caused By an Eruptive Magnetic Flux Rope
status_evidence.snippet: Observations provided clear evidence that emerging magnetic flux ropes may be a common trigger of bubbles and suggested a new mechanism of plumes in addition to Rayleigh–Taylor instability and reconnection.
status_evidence.claim: Emerging flux ropes are still being proposed as a trigger of bubbles and plumes, indicating ongoing debate.

status_evidence.title: Mass Motion in a Prominence Bubble Revealing a Kinked Flux Rope Configuration
status_evidence.snippet: Both the Kelvin–Helmholtz and Rayleigh–Taylor instabilities are present... plumes were conjectured to be driven by reconnection at the magnetic separator outlining the bubble.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple competing mechanisms for plume formation remain under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Response of the solar atmosphere to flux emergence — With emergence-driven prominence formation
status_evidence.snippet: 2025 modeling study of flux emergence and prominence formation.
status_evidence.claim: The interplay between emerging flux and prominence material is still being modeled in 2025.
